content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral table, and all six figure briefs, tracing each limitation and each drawn feature to an affirmative inventor passage.

input.summary: Full ledger built and traced. All 20 claims (1-10 device, 11-15 system, 16-20 method) were traced limitation by limitation to affirmative inventor passages: rigid base with first/second sides, motor coupled to the first side, air-extraction mechanism such as a vacuum pump coupled to the first side and in fluid communication with a chamber on the second side, rigid low-friction loop or skirt at the perimeter of the second side (plastic, metal, PTFE, combinations of rigid materials), non-sealing perimeter that restricts but does not stop inflow, continuous extraction maintaining sub-atmospheric chamber pressure, resulting pressure differential holding the device without operator downward force, all-rigid vibration path with no elastomer/foam/resilient mount, sliding to successive areas while the hold is maintained, guiding handles, and the rope/wire/cable pulling element with decoupled position-versus-hold control (disclosure.md throughout). Claim 10, the FIG. 6 embodiment, the autonomous-movement recital in the Field, and the stirring-element paragraph in the detailed description trace to the single affirmative USER passage "we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion"; the surrounding operational USER messages (resume, rebuild, regenerate, tighten the Field) were treated as instructions, not disclosure. All seventeen numerals (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48) were checked: each is defined once, each carries one meaning in every figure brief and in the description, each appears in at least one brief, and no numeral appears in a brief without a table entry; the 28-32 gap is an unused range only. All six figure briefs were checked against the Brief Description of the Drawings and the detailed description: the 2-2 and 4-4 designations are carried identically in FIG. 3's annotation instructions, in the FIG. 2 and FIG. 4 view lines, and in draft/07-drawings.md; omissions for clarity match in every case (motor and handle in FIG. 2, motor and extraction mechanism in FIG. 5, covering element and internal parts in FIG. 6). Depiction conventions were assessed against the substantive-geometry rule: the rectangular slab, ring plan form, band width and depth, block order and spacing, flat lower end of the bearing face, equal-depth bedded layers, two-block stirring count, cord attachment place, and the schematic communication gap through the base are each declared schematic inside the brief that contains them, each corresponds to a part the inventor affirmatively disclosed (rigid loop at the perimeter, fluid communication between the extraction mechanism and the chamber, bearing contact on the tile, tile bedded on bonding material over a substrate, cord connected to the device, stirring elements added to the device), and none verbalizes an undisclosed depth, taper, angle, runout, port construction, or contact topology. No convention leaked into the application text: draft/07-drawings.md and the detailed description use only "shown schematically" and contain no "by way of example", "any closed outline", or renderer-justifying embodiment. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction to a person, unresolved alternative, or internal comment remains in any of the ten draft sections; the [REF:...] tokens are citation markers for the separate citation review. The abstract is 145 words. One verified internal inconsistency was found and is reported: the FIG. 5 paragraph of the Brief Description of the Drawings recites the perimeter member as shown schematically, but the authoritative FIG. 5 brief neither names its band as the perimeter member nor assigns numeral 24 on that sheet. No unsupported technical assertion was found in the claims, the description, the abstract, or any figure brief.

findings.title: Brief Description recites the perimeter member for FIG. 5, but the authoritative FIG. 5 brief neither names nor numbers it
findings.detail: The Brief Description of the Drawings tells the reader that FIG. 5 shows the perimeter member schematically. The authoritative FIG. 5 brief draws only "a band that runs round its underside", never identifies that band as the perimeter member, and lists only numerals 10, 36 and 46 for the sheet, so numeral 24 does not appear on FIG. 5. Every other figure paragraph in draft/07-drawings.md enumerates exactly the parts its brief identifies and numbers (FIG. 1: 10, 12, 18, 20, 24, 36, 44; FIG. 2: 12, 14, 20, 22, 24, 36; FIG. 3: 16, 24; FIG. 4: 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42; FIG. 6: 10, 48). FIG. 5 is the single mismatch. This is a text-versus-brief inconsistency only; the underlying subject matter (a perimeter loop bearing on the tile) is fully supported by the disclosure, and no unsupported structure is being drawn.
findings.evidence: draft/07-drawings.md: "FIG. 5 is a perspective view of a second embodiment in which a flexible pulling element is connected to the device ... the vibration device, the perimeter member, the covering element, the flexible pulling element and the connection of the flexible pulling element to the vibration device being shown schematically." FIG. 5 brief: "the machine as one plain rectangular body standing on a band that runs round its underside, the band alone touching the tile" and "**Numerals appearing on this figure:** 10, 36, 46". Compare FIG. 1 brief, which does name the same feature: "The perimeter member 24 is the band beneath the slab."
findings.fix: In draft/07-drawings.md, delete the two words ", the perimeter member" from the FIG. 5 paragraph, so it reads: "... the vibration motor and the air-extraction mechanism being omitted for clarity, and the vibration device, the covering element, the flexible pulling element and the connection of the flexible pulling element to the vibration device being shown schematically." Change nothing in the FIG. 5 brief, in any other figure paragraph, in the detailed description, or in the numeral table.
